guide.summary: Harbour museums, island fortress, city museums and bouillabaisse tables, with breakfast, bakeries, coffee and hotel bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan around closing days: the Mucem closes on Tuesdays, the city museums open Tuesday to Sunday only, and from 28 September to 31 March the Château d'If closes on Mondays and does not open in bad weather.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Mucem and its Café du Fort close on Tuesdays, while the Vieille Charité, Musée Cantini, mac and other city museums open Tuesday to Sunday. In winter the Château d'If also closes on Mondays.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: A same-day Mucem ticket, 11 euros full rate, covers every exhibition in J4 and Fort Saint-Jean, and the outdoor areas are free. Château d'If entry is 7 euros, with the boat crossing sold separately.

toolkit.label: Booking
toolkit.copy: Le Miramar, Chez Fonfon, Sépia and AM par Alexandre Mazzia all take bookings through their own sites, and AM serves only Wednesday to Saturday. At Cosquer Méditerranée the last visit slot is an hour and a half before closing.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Children under 3 cannot take the cave tour at Cosquer Méditerranée, though the auditorium and gallery are open to them. The Château d'If does not open in bad weather.

guide.dek: Put the Mucem and the Château d'If on separate days, and check closing days before you book a table.
intro: Marseille's harbour front is anchored by the Mucem, which you visit across two sites, the J4 building and Fort Saint-Jean. Both open 10:00 to 19:00 in May, June, September and October, 10:00 to 20:00 in July and August and 10:00 to 18:00 from November to April, and both close on Tuesdays. One same-day ticket, 11 euros at full rate, covers every exhibition, while the outdoor areas are free. A new exhibition, The Taste of images, opens on 28 October 2026. Next door on the J4 Esplanade, Cosquer Méditerranée opens every day, with its last visit slot an hour and a half before closing.

The city museums open Tuesday to Sunday, 9:00 to 18:00. At the Centre de la Vieille Charité in Le Panier, Adrien Vescovi's Dormir comme le soleil runs until 10 January 2027, and Louisa Babari's Voix Publiques is spread across the Vieille Charité, the mac and the Musée Cantini until 3 January 2027. In the Palais Longchamp, the Muséum d'histoire naturelle shows Dinosaures de Provence until 20 June 2027 and pauses from 12:30 to 13:30, while the Musée des Beaux-Arts fills the opposite wing. The Musée d'Histoire de Marseille is closed until further notice.

For the water, boats to the Château d'If leave from the Vieux-Port at the lower end of the Canebière. Entry is 7 euros, and the crossing is paid separately. From 28 September to 31 March the château opens 10:00 to 17:15 and closes on Mondays, and it does not open in bad weather. Inland, La Friche la Belle de Mai at 41 rue Jobin hosts the Biennale des Imaginaires Numériques until 13 December 2026, and its restaurant, Les Grandes Tables, serves lunch Monday to Saturday. Frac Sud on boulevard de Dunkerque opens Wednesday to Sunday afternoons.

For bouillabaisse, Le Miramar on the quai du Port serves Tuesday to Sunday, and Chez Fonfon in the Vallon des Auffes opens every day and says its fish are caught daily by its own pointus. AM par Alexandre Mazzia serves Wednesday to Saturday only. For mornings, Mama Shelter on rue de la Loubière serves breakfast daily from 7:00 to 11:00 and a Sunday brunch from 11:30 to 15:30. La Pâtisserie des Marseillais on Grand Rue closes on Mondays, and Le Four des Navettes on rue Sainte sells its navettes as a Marseille tradition dating from 1781.
summaryCards: Start with the Mucem and Fort Saint-Jean on any day but Tuesday, then take a boat from the Vieux-Port to the Château d'If.
Have breakfast at Mama Shelter, served daily from 7:00 to 11:00, then pick up navettes at Le Four des Navettes on rue Sainte.
Check closing days: AM par Alexandre Mazzia serves Wednesday to Saturday, Sépia is closed at weekends and Le Miramar serves Tuesday to Sunday.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several sites could not be read: the Calanques National Park site (DNS failure), Notre-Dame de la Garde (the .fr domain now shows unrelated casino content and the .com refused the connection), L'Épuisette, Les Halles de la Major (expired certificate), La Caravelle (503), Les Bords de Mer, Abbaye Saint-Victor (403), Deep Coffee Roasters (429) and Carry Nation (error page); the domains listed for Risette and Café Coogee no longer belong to the cafés. Le Petit Nice, the Capian bar and the Dantès Skylounge publish no hours, Le Four des Navettes publishes no hours, and Sépia, Julis, AM par Alexandre Mazzia and Le Four des Navettes show no dated 2026 content beyond live booking or shop pages. The Mucem pages read give entrance locations but no street number. Cosquer Méditerranée labels its published hours as 2024. Torréfaction Noailles' Canebière page does not say whether coffee is served on site. Notices that end within two weeks, such as the city museums' 1 November closure, Frac Sud's strike-weekend closure and Mama Shelter's Halloween events, were left out of the guide copy. No official page was found for a food market, so markets are not covered.
